newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt, EU say premature for Mideast peace summit.
newsitem.headline: Egypt, EU say premature for Mideast peace summit.

text.p: Egyptian Foreign Minister Amr Moussa said on Monday any consideration of a mini-summit to help revive stalled Middle East peace talks could wait until Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat met Israeli President Ezer Weizman.

Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak said last week that he would be willing to hold a meeting between Jordan, Egypt, the Palestinians and Israel if Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu backs down on a decision to build a controversial Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

"It's too early for such talk. Let's just see the results of Arafat's meeting with the Israeli president tomorrow (Tuesday)," Moussa told reporters after meeting European Union envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos in Cairo.

Moratinos said on Monday it was premature to think about holding a four-way summit at this stage. "A summit could help (break the deadlock) but I think it is very premature. We have to work very hard before we have such a summit."
Jordanian Prime Minister Abdul-Salam al-Majali said in Doha on Monday that his country welcomed such a summit.
Peace talks have been snagged for seven weeks over Israel's settlement decision. Arafat met Mubarak in Cairo on Monday to consult on ways to revive the talks ahead of his meeting with Weizman.
Jordan and Egypt, who have peace treaties with Israel, often mediate in negotiations between the Jewish state and its Arab neighbours.
